raw: 50.1 Executive Order 12333: United States Intelligence Activities[^221]
teaching_note: The inherited citation ageint221 identifies PPD-28, not Executive Order 12333; retain that identity without treating one presidential instrument as the other [@ageint221]. For EO 12333, the existing ODNI text explicitly states amendments in 2003, 2004, and 2008, while the NARA codification displays older DCI-era institutional wording; neither an old page nor an official host alone certifies the current consolidated legal position [@official_eo_12333_odni_text; @official_odni_eo_12333]. The ODNI version's section 2.3 places collection, retention, and dissemination concerning United States persons within specified approved procedures, so its public-information/consent category is not blanket permission for any actor or activity. Application requires current text/status, governed actor, activity, territory/data nexus, time, scope and implementing procedures, reviewed by an authorized legal specialist; this lesson provides no collection authority or legal advice.
title: Executive Order 12333: Version Limits and the Distinct PPD-28 Source

teaching_note: A statute, executive instrument, judicial authorization, agency directive, voluntary standard, ethical recommendation, and local policy have different sources of force and scope; an analytic-quality directive cannot supply surveillance authority. The inherited ICD 203/index citations do not establish current FISA provisions, amendments, effective dates, or approvals [@ageint297; @ageint298]. A completed fictional applicability record uses actor 'training team T', activity 'summarize synthetic cards offline', territory 'fictional J', date 'exercise day 10', policy P1 'effective day 1; permits only synthetic classroom processing', and draft statute S2 'proposed; no effective date': P1 permits that exercise only, and S2 supplies no operative authority. A proposed real-message upload is held because actual jurisdiction, applicable current statute, actor competence, data rights, provider/location boundary, and required approvals are absent; counsel/privacy review must resolve them, and no defensive purpose or instructor signature waives the hold.
title: FISA and Surveillance Law

teaching_note: An index locates documents; it does not establish that a listed version remains operative, applies to the proposed actor, or authorizes the proposed activity [@ageint006; @ageint298]. Record the issuing authority, document type, revision, effective date, supersession status, applicability, and exact provision before interpretation. ICD 203 addresses analytic standards, so citing it for uncertainty and sourcing is different from citing a lawful basis to obtain or disclose data [@ageint297]. If the required current instrument is missing, the correct disposition is unsupported/hold rather than an inferred permission.
title: Intelligence Community Directives: Index Provenance versus Current Text

teaching_note: The inherited 'Classification Guide' description is not treated as a verified current rulebook: the cited PDF's document type, date, completeness, and operative status require readable source confirmation [@ageint222]. Distinguish a public historical review record, authority to classify or declassify, a handling/control marking, and permission to disclose a particular item. In a fictional exercise, a publicly posted cover sheet accompanies an unverified attachment description; the reviewer permits discussion of the approved synthetic cover-sheet text only and holds any claim that the attachment is public or releasable. Removing a label, finding a public URL, or receiving a classroom request cannot supply the missing disclosure decision.
title: CIA/NARA Classification Record: Document-type and Version Verification

raw: 50.5 Allied Legal Frameworks: RIPA, Investigatory Powers Act, GDPR
teaching_note: RIPA, the Investigatory Powers Act, and GDPR are not interchangeable authorities or a complete allied-law map; a data-protection instrument is not surveillance authorization. The inherited US directive/index citations do not support detailed UK/EU legal rules, so current provisions, amendments, territorial/material scope, commencement or application dates, exclusions, and responsible decision-makers remain prerequisites rather than asserted answers [@ageint298; @ageint297]. For fictional record U, actor T proposes sending a 'public' dataset to a provider in an unknown territory: source permission, lawful basis, affected data categories, transfers, recipient powers, and current applicable instruments are unknown, so the outcome is no ingestion or transfer pending specialist review. Consent is not a universal lawful basis, public availability is not permission, and a claimed national-security exception does not establish the absence of all other duties.
title: Selected UK/EU Instruments: Separate Applicability Questions, Not an Allied-law Map

teaching_note: International-law analysis distinguishes treaty obligations, customary-law claims, domestic implementation, and nonbinding recommendations; a treaty's signature, entry into force, and application to a particular actor/activity are separate questions. The inherited analytic directive sources cannot establish international-law permission, universal allied agreement, or a jurisdiction-specific remedy [@ageint297; @ageint298]. A fictional instrument register records treaty K as 'signed by J; ratification, entry into force for J, reservations, domestic effect, and activity scope unknown', and the legal reviewer therefore holds the claimed authority instead of treating signature as universal obligation or permission. Use Section [@sec:analytic-workflow] to retain those missing links and reopen review when actor, purpose, territory, recipient, or instrument status changes.
title: The International Law of Intelligence
